Paragraph:
Translation: The soul can never be cut into pieces by any weapon, nor can he be burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.

Purport (Excerpt): All kinds of weapons, swords, flames, rains, tornadoes, etc., are unable to kill the spirit soul... Nonetheless, the soul can never be cut into pieces, nor annihilated by any number of weapons, regardless of scientific devices. Nor was it ever possible to cut the individual souls from the original Soul.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is standing on a battlefield surrounded by weapons meant to cut, burn, and destroy. He is terrified of the physical devastation about to occur.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna systematically negates the threat of every elemental weapon (earth/swords, fire, water, air/wind) against the soul. He asserts the absolute invulnerability of the core self.
Outcome/Resolution: The psychological threat posed by the surrounding arsenal is neutralized because the weapons cannot touch what actually matters.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.psychological Invulnerability: An impenetrable sense of core safety

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sanatana (Eternal, indivisible parts of the Supreme)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The soul exists beyond the influence of material elements. Weapons are made of matter (earth, fire, water, air) and can only affect other matter. The spirit soul is of a higher, transcendental nature, making it completely immune to any material interaction or destruction.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse builds profound trauma resistance. By visualizing the core identity as completely immune to being cut, burned, or broken, an individual develops an internal locus of ultimate safety. Even if the body is subjected to extreme violence or trauma, the psyche can remain anchored in the belief that the true 'self' remains completely untouched and whole.
